Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 02/09/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 210 as introduced could increase receipts to the State General Fund by an undetermined amount, dependent upon the funds remaining from criminal asset forfeiture sales, resulting from a criminal conviction for a drug related offense, after disbursements for: (1) victim restitution; (2) payments for outstanding liens, mortgages, or filed security interests in the forfeited property; (3) payments for reasonable costs associated with the sale and maintenance of the forfeited property; (4) reimbursements to the seizing law enforcement agency for non-personnel operating costs; and (5) reimbursements to the prosecuting authority for non-personnel operating costs.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 04/26/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 210 as passed the Senate provides further for asset forfeiture proceedings, including that the court may award proceeds from the sale of such forfeiture to the seizing agency and/or the prosecuting authority. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Date: 04/28/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 210 as amended and reported by the Committee on State Government provides further for asset forfeiture proceedings, including that the court may award proceeds from the sale of such forfeiture to the seizing agency and/or the prosecuting authority. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Pringle
Analyst: Jessica Perez
Date: 04/12/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 326 as passed the House of Representatives would allow the Alabama Board of Registration of Foresters to meet more often than once per month which could increase the obligations of the Professional Foresters Fund by an estimated $1,250 for each meeting of the board.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
